system_prompt_style.evidence_quote: When the Responses API receives a prompt, it assembles model context: user prompt, prior conversation state, and tool instructions.

system_prompt_style.note: Skill metadata also injected before prompt.

env_context_strategy.evidence_quote: A better pattern is to stage resources in the container file system and let the model decide what to open, parse, or transform with shell commands.

context_compaction.evidence_quote: we added native compaction in the Responses API, designed to align with how the model behaves and how it's been trained.
context_compaction.evidence_locator: paper (blog) sec. When the context window gets full: compaction
context_compaction.note: Per-command output cap preserving beginning and end also enforced. Mismatch: native compaction produces a summary-like encrypted compaction item.

observation_format.evidence_quote: the API multiplexes those streams back into structured tool outputs as context
observation_format.evidence_locator: paper (blog) sec. Orchestrating the agent loop
observation_format.note: Shell output streamed; format of structured tool outputs not detailed.

tool_call_format.evidence_quote: If it chooses shell execution, it returns one or more shell commands to Responses API service.
tool_call_format.evidence_locator: paper (blog) sec. Orchestrating the agent loop
tool_call_format.note: Hosted shell tool; custom tools yield control to client.

tool_count.evidence_quote: We'll start with the shell tool—the simplest way to see this loop in action
tool_count.note: Only the shell tool described for this configuration; exact tool list not reported.

edit_primitive.evidence_quote: Built on familiar Unix tooling, our shell tool can do anything you'd expect, with utilities like grep, curl, and awk available out of the box.
edit_primitive.note: No dedicated edit tool described; edits via shell.

loop_primitives.evidence_quote: The Responses API repeats this loop until the model returns a completion without additional shell commands.
loop_primitives.evidence_locator: paper (blog) sec. Orchestrating the agent loop

planning_granularity.evidence_quote: The model proposes steps and commands; the platform runs them in an isolated environment

multi_agent_topology.evidence_quote: We need an orchestrator to get model output, invoke tools, and pass the tool response back to the model in a loop, until the task is complete.
multi_agent_topology.evidence_locator: paper (blog) sec. Orchestrating the agent loop

long_term_memory.evidence_quote: Developers upload and store skill folders as versioned bundles, which can later be retrieved by skill ID.

filesystem_access.evidence_quote: Inside the container, the model can read files, query databases, and access external systems under network policy controls.

network_policy.evidence_quote: All outbound network requests flow through a centralized policy layer that enforces allowlists and access controls while keeping traffic observable.

guardrails.evidence_quote: The model and container only see placeholders, while raw secret values stay outside model-visible context and only get applied for approved destinations.

target_domain.evidence_quote: running services, requesting data from APIs, or generating more useful artifacts like spreadsheets or reports
